newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Five police killed in Bogota explosion.
newsitem.headline: Five police killed in Bogota explosion.

text.p: At least five policemen were killed on Tuesday in a powerful explosion that tore through an area just outside a police station in a working-class district on the southwest outskirts of Bogota, authorities said.

Metropolitan Police commander Teodoro Campo said the agents were killed, and an unknown number were seriously injured, when the explosion occurred in the back of a truck that was being searched for suspected contraband goods.
Campo, who spoke in an interview with the Radionet news network, said the explosion was caused by some sort of "a device" stashed somewhere in the back of the lighweight truck.

He fell short of calling it a bomb and said the explosion was not necessarily believed to have been intentional, or directed against the police, since the truck had been towed from the main square in the Fontibon district.
The Radionet news network said at least nine police were injured in the explosion, which occurred at about 5:20 p.m. (2220 GMT).
Radionet also said six police officers had died in the explosion, which partly destroyed the local police station.
